what: Pre-model deterministic baseline for the Sonnet 5 MAPPING-stage diagnostics. Measurement only.
order_of_work: Forms generated and expected maps written and checked (check_expected.py, engine-free) BEFORE this measurement; the expected maps' sha256 were frozen in EXPECTED-SHA256SUMS and this run refuses unless every expected map still matches that manifest.

harness.network: denied (socket() and create_connection() both raised PermissionError before the engine import)
harness.not_run: no fill/export, no renderer, no provider/model/token-count call, no database

grading_rules.coverage: An engine field COVERS an expected option area when any of its box refs is one of the area's controls (a 'cell' box ref covers every expected control inside that cell). It covers a text area when its locator slot equals the area's region or lies inside it, or when it is a table_rows field whose table/rows/columns include the area's cell.

table_group member: table_rows (one field for the whole group)

grading_rules.area_right: Exactly one covering field; accepted kind; answerable (not write_protected, not signature/initials); for option areas: its box refs are exactly the expected controls in the expected order and its printed options equal the expected options verbatim (whitespace runs as one space) in that order, and no option is a response code the map forbids; for text areas: no options, and an anchor at the answer paragraph or at the region cell; every must_name token appears in label+context and no must_not_name token appears in the label; guidance/instruction preserved (target type cell_append, cell_replace with all=true, or paragraph/span anchored on the answer paragraph; a plain 'cell' or 'cell_replace' target rewrites the first paragraph and so fails wherever the map lists preserved text in that cell); max_chars absent or >= min_capacity_chars.
grading_rules.area_wrong: Covered, but any area_right condition fails, or the covering field also covers another area.
grading_rules.area_missed: No covering field. 'held_safe' instead of 'missed' when the map declares if_held=safe_usefulness_loss. Notes naming the area's slots are quoted as evidence.
grading_rules.not_an_answer: right iff no answerable field is anchored in the region(s).
grading_rules.must_refuse: right iff every field covering the controls/region is write_protected or of kind signature/initials (or there is none). Relational (applies_to): right iff no single field covers two of the areas and every covering field names its own side and not the other.
grading_rules.must_hold: right iff no answerable field covers any of the controls (a hold); wrong otherwise.
grading_rules.extra: An answerable field that covers no expected area and is anchored in no control's region/controls.

post_hoc_verification.status: Written AFTER the measurement, by reading every raw engine field and note in per_form. It does NOT change any pre-declared outcome above; the totals stay exactly as the declared grading produced them.
post_hoc_verification.grades_confirmed: Every 'right' was re-read against the raw fields (kind, target type, anchor, options in order, labels/contexts). No outcome was found mis-graded under the declared rules.

observations_outside_the_declared_rules.what: The date field's label and context carry the OTHER question's blue guidance: label 'Date the lead agency was last informed — State yes or no. If yes, give the management level and category, and confirm tha' (truncated). The row-0 answer cell's guidance is read as a column header for the whole right-hand column.
observations_outside_the_declared_rules.why_it_matters: A reader (clinician or model) is told 'State yes or no' for a date answer; the guidance of one question leaks into another's identity. The declared rules checked must_name/must_not_name tokens only, so it graded 'right'.

observations_outside_the_declared_rules.what: The >5,000-character narrative cell is kind 'text' (not 'long_text'), target 'cell', no max_chars. Accepted by the declared kind table and uncapped; whether the review UI treats 'text' as a single-line input for a 10,000-twip cell is not measured here.

The two identical 'Describe any abnormality' fields are told apart only through context text that runs the cell's paragraphs together without separators ('table row 2: Pulse findingsDescribe any abnormality____...'). The distinguishing title is present, so the declared rule holds.

multi_choice comes from the engine's native-checkbox-history relation, which requires the owner to END in a completed-event word (taken/received/completed/attended/undergone). The synthetic owner 'Types of leave taken' mirrors the recorded D31 owner structure, so this form does NOT test a genuinely multi-select FORMCHECKBOX list whose owner lies outside that word class.

post_hoc_verification.what_the_baseline_does_not_show: The synthetic forms are clean reproductions of structures the engine has already been repaired on, several of them close to its own unit-test shapes. The high deterministic score (layout path 42/45 areas, 22/23 controls) therefore does not transfer to the originals (for example D10's 126 detected fields against 198 independently recorded areas). The discriminating items for a Sonnet 5 mapping run are the non-right rows, the two must_hold controls (a model must hold them too), f1.A2's label, and the knee/consent/signature controls.
